confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on four web searches of crowd-sourced cost-of-living data. These sources were Citycost, Oysterlist and Expatistan for Naha, Expatica/Numbeo for Okinawa Prefecture, and Numbeo's Japan page dated November 2026. I also looked at one undated izakaya menu in Naha that charged JPY 390 for draft beer and JPY 490 for a highball. The sources disagree: estimates for an inexpensive meal run from about JPY 930 to JPY 1,570, and beer ranges from shop-level prices to about USD 4. I converted at about JPY 155-160 per USD, which is the rate the source pages imply. Beer is set a little above the cited draught averages to reflect a typical izakaya serving. The searches found no aggregated prices for cocktails or wine. Those two anchors use the local relationship to beer and highball prices plus general knowledge of Okinawa bar pricing, so they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not checked against live listings. They allow for July being peak summer season in Okinawa, which raises hotel rates noticeably, so they are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Naha is a mid-sized Japanese regional city and resort gateway. Restaurant and drink prices are roughly at or slightly below national averages, which puts them below Tokyo and similar to Fukuoka or Sapporo. Accommodation is set higher than in comparable regional cities to account for July beach-season demand.
